public_prompt: Quarterly availability is published as 99.95%, obtained by averaging 40 services' individual percentages with equal contribution. A customer disputes it. The reading so far: the published figure is the platform's availability. Report the availability a customer actually met.
observable_resources: sre/service-availability.csv — 40 services, individual quarterly availability from 99.20% to 100.00%; the equal-contribution average is 99.95%
sre/service-volume.csv — the lowest-scoring service carries 71% of all calls; 28 services carry under 0.5% of calls each
sre/customer-claim.md — a customer reports 17.3 hours of failed calls across the 2,160-hour quarter, which matches 99.2% on the service they use
sre/report-method.md — the published figure adds the 40 percentages and divides by 40
closure:sla-credit-denial — closed; refuses credits on the 99.95% figure
closure:enterprise-renewal-terms — closed; derived from closure:sla-credit-denial, renews on the published figure
closure:status-page-update-standard — closed; requires a public note within 30 minutes of an outage; rests on the communications standard, not on how the quarterly figure is combined
closure:health-check-interval — closed; fixes the one-minute probe interval; rests on the monitoring standard, not on how the 40 services are combined

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff availability is recomputed with each service contributing in proportion to the calls it carries, giving roughly 99.4% or worse, and the answer states that an equal-contribution average lets 28 near-idle services mask the one service carrying 71% of calls. FAIL if the answer defends 99.95%, reports only the worst service's figure, or proposes adding more health checks.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the equal-contribution framing denies the credit; the customer's 17.3 hours is exactly what the dominant service's 99.2% predicts.
